:::{#exm-moment-die}
#### Raw moments of a die roll

Let $X$ be the number shown by one roll of a fair six-sided die,
so that $\P(X = x) = 1/6$ for each $x \in \set{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6}$.
The first [raw moment](#def-moment) is the [expectation](expectation.qmd#def-expectation) $\E{X}$,
and the second is $\E{X^2}$:

$$
\ba
\E{X}
&= \sum_{x=1}^{6} x \cd \frac{1}{6}
&& \text{(definition of expectation)} \\
&= \frac{21}{6}
&& \text{(} 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 21 \text{)} \\
&= \frac{7}{2}
&& \text{(simplify)} \\
\E{X^2}
&= \sum_{x=1}^{6} x^2 \cd \frac{1}{6}
&& \text{(expectation of a function of a discrete random variable)} \\
&= \frac{91}{6}
&& \text{(} 1 + 4 + 9 + 16 + 25 + 36 = 91 \text{)}
\ea
$$

<!-- no-figure: the example computes single numbers, not data -->

:::
